summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of neurogenic bladder, paraplegia, and chronic urinary tract infections was admitted with a one-week history of fevers and flank pain, initially concerning for pyelonephritis. She had recently been to the emergency department and prescribed Bactrim but did not take it, managing symptoms with ibuprofen. On admission, she received IV gentamicin and was started on vancomycin and ceftriaxone. Her Foley catheter was replaced, and a wound on the plantar surface of the right fourth toe was evaluated with X-ray and inflammatory markers, which showed no evidence of bone infection. Urine culture revealed mixed bacterial flora consistent with contamination, and blood cultures were negative. Antibiotics were discontinued after 24 hours of being afebrile, and she remained stable. Her pain was attributed to chronic musculoskeletal and neuropathic causes. She was discharged home with a short course of Percocet for pain, adjusted psychiatric medications, and instructions to care for her toe wound with a protective boot. Follow-up was advised for any signs of infection.
